hooks.name: Assert.IQ Dreaming - session start gate
hooks.description: If the dual gate is met (>= min_hours AND >= min_sessions since the last dream), nudge the user to run /dream. Never blocks.

action.command: R='${WORKSPACE_ROOT}'; S="$R/.assert-iq/dreaming/scripts/dream-gate.sh"; [ -f "$S" ] || { R='__PACK_ROOT__'; S="$R/.assert-iq/dreaming/scripts/dream-gate.sh"; }; [ -f "$S" ] || exit 0; AIQ_PACK_ROOT="$R" AIQ_HOOK_OUTPUT=plain bash "$S"

hooks.name: Assert.IQ Dreaming - record session
hooks.description: Increment the session counter and append a line to the daily memory log when a turn ends.

action.command: R='${WORKSPACE_ROOT}'; S="$R/.assert-iq/dreaming/scripts/dream-record-session.sh"; [ -f "$S" ] || { R='__PACK_ROOT__'; S="$R/.assert-iq/dreaming/scripts/dream-record-session.sh"; }; [ -f "$S" ] || exit 0; AIQ_PACK_ROOT="$R" AIQ_HOOK_OUTPUT=plain bash "$S"

hooks.name: Assert.IQ Dreaming - capture waking notes
hooks.description: Kiro-only content capture. Kiro's Stop payload carries no transcript_path and Kiro writes no transcript file, so the shell recorder above can only emit a heartbeat. The agent has the finished turn in context, so it is the capture layer here -- the Kiro-native equivalent of transcript mining on Claude Code and Copilot.

action.prompt:
Assert.IQ Dreaming - waking note capture. Do this silently: do not mention it in your reply to the user.

Review the turn that just finished and decide whether it produced any DURABLE fact worth remembering in a later session. Most turns do not. If nothing durable happened, write nothing at all and stop -- an empty turn is the normal case, and inventing signal is worse than recording none.

If it did, append AT MOST 3 lines to today's daily log at `.assert-iq/memory/logs/<YYYY>/<MM>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` (UTC). Create the file with a `# Daily log <YYYY-MM-DD>` heading only if it does not exist. Append only -- never rewrite or delete existing lines.

One line per fact, exactly this shape:
- <UTC ISO8601>Z note[<CATEGORY>]: <one sentence>

CATEGORY is one of:
  DECISION   - a choice made and the reason, where the reason still matters later
  CORRECTION - the user redirected or overruled; record what they wanted instead
  GOTCHA     - a trap, failure mode, or environment quirk that cost time and would again
  PREFERENCE - a standing instruction about how to work in this repo

Rules for the sentence:
- Absolute dates only. Never 'today', 'yesterday', or 'last week'.
- Paraphrase. Never paste code, secrets, tokens, credentials or PII.
- Specific enough to act on months later; a fact, not a summary of what you did.
- Preserve the user's wording when recording a decision or a correction.

Write ONLY under `.assert-iq/memory/`. Never modify `.github/instructions/*`, skills, source, or config -- those are the immutable rules tier and outrank anything recorded here.
